tools.name: aspsms_check_credits
tools.description: Show the remaining ASPSMS credit balance of the account. Read-only. Calls the ASPSMS CheckCredits method.

tools.name: aspsms_inquire_delivery_notifications
tools.description: Read the delivery status of SMS messages sent with a transaction reference (set when the SMS was sent). Read-only. Calls InquireDeliveryNotifications.

tools.name: aspsms_send_sms
tools.description: Send one or more real SMS messages and spend the account's ASPSMS credits. Sends cannot be recalled. Confirm the recipients and the text with the user before calling. Calls SendTextSMS.

tools.name: aspsms_unlock_originator
tools.description: Unlock a phone number as the sender, using the unlock code that ASPSMS sent to that number. Changes the account's sender settings. Calls UnlockOriginator.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "aspsms_send_sms" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Send one or more real SMS messages and spend the account's ASPSMS credits. Sends cannot be recalled. Confirm the recipients and the text with the user before ca…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: aspsms_inquire_delivery_notifications · Public sink: aspsms_inquire_delivery_notifications, aspsms_send_sms.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: aspsms_inquire_delivery_notifications · Public sink: aspsms_inquire_delivery_notifications, aspsms_send_sms

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
